reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that heterogeneous treatment effect (HTE) estimation in observational studies benefits most from local centering of the treatment variable using estimated propensity scores. This approach reduces bias by adjusting for confounding at each node during tree construction. The mathematical structure of the estimator E[Y|x,w] = μ(x) + τ(x)(w − π̂(x)) embeds this idea directly into the loss function. Simultaneous splitting on both prognostic (μ) and predictive (τ) components enhances accuracy further, especially when outcome centering is suboptimal. The framework supports generalization to non-Gaussian outcomes via transformation forests, allowing for robust modeling of skewed or censored data such as interval-censored blood loss. The key dualities lie between causal inference and machine learning: while causal forests rely on explicit centering, model-based forests allow flexible modeling of complex distributions. Both approaches converge under additive L2 regularization, providing a unified basis for empirical estimation. Failure modes include poor propensity estimation, lack of overlap, and misalignment between prognostic and predictive signals.
